svg.aria-label: A revision map for the final exam, covering weeks 10 to 16. Across the top, three boxes state the spine of the second half. One: a control has to sit at a boundary — the check runs on the server, per request, per object — demonstrated in week 10, where /api/users/3/orders answers 401, then 403, then 200, all decided server-side. Two: a control has to be on by default — the safe path is the only path, not a flag you pass — demonstrated in week 11, where the bounds checks in safe.rs make the stack overflow impossible rather than merely harder. Three: a control has to fail closed — on error it denies and logs the reason, never the secret — demonstrated in week 15, where port 8090 fails open while port 8091 denies and logs, CWE-636. The three boxes are joined by plus signs: all three, or it is not a control. Below, a table gives one row per week: its OWASP or CWE tag, its core idea, and the first-half week it builds on. Week 10, API security, API1 BOLA, API3 mass assignment, API4 unrestricted resource consumption — these are authorization flaws, not input flaws; /api/users/3/orders returns any user's row. It builds on week 6 authorization: deny by default, now enforced per request and per object. Week 11, memory safety and exploitation, CWE-121 and CWE-787, plus CWE-134 format string — untrusted bytes reach the stack through strcpy in parse_input, at offset 72. It builds on week 4 injection: input reaches a sink, and here the sink is the stack. Week 12, supply chain, A03 and A08 with CWE-1357 — you did not write most of your code, and the public look-alike acme-internal-utils version 99.0.0 wins the resolution. It builds on week 2 secure SDLC: a flaw ships unless something scans it, and now that scanner is SCA, an SBOM and cosign. Week 13, cloud and container, A02 with CWE-732 and CWE-798 — the flaw is in the configuration, not the code: Dockerfile.insecure uses the latest tag, runs as root, bakes ENV API_TOKEN, and the IAM policy allows Action star on Resource star. It builds on week 3 cryptography: a key baked into an image is not a secret. Week 14, AI and LLM security, LLM01, LLM02 and LLM05 — the prompt is not a security control; override it and the FLAG comes out. It builds on week 5 cross-site scripting: model output is untrusted input, and must be escaped before it reaches the page. Week 15, DevSecOps gates, A09, A10 and CWE-636 — Semgrep, Trivy and Gitleaks run on every pull request, and port 8090 fails open while port 8091 returns 403. It builds on week 2 tooling again: the same scanners, except now they are allowed to stop the build. Week 16, capstone, all weeks, with a CWE and OWASP mapping required — against your own application: attack, root cause, fix, then SBOM, signature and CI gate. It builds on week 1 threat modelling: the data-flow diagram you drew in week 1 is deliverable number one. Small numbered circles on the week 10, week 11 and week 15 rows mark the week that demonstrates each of the three spine properties.
